pr_title: Allow vaulted string to be used as actual strings (#73054)
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Multiple places in the code base expect actual `str` types and
refuse to work with objects that can be treated as strings.
This commit lets `AnsibleVaultEncryptedUnicode` deceive those
places by faking to be a `str`.

Fixes #73054

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
`AnsibleVaultEncryptedUnicode`

fwiw, using the `urlencode` filter with a vault-encrypted string now raises a `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)`.

This happens because Jinja performs runtime type checking on the value to be encoded, and if `isinstance(val, str)` is false and the value is also not a `dict`, it assumes that it's an iterable of `(key, value)` tuples, which is why we get that error.
https://github.com/pallets/jinja/blob/52843b5cbf635b37a82ac0b6c901921a8ee076ff/src/jinja2/filters.py#L144-L172
is there any workaround for this issue? I need to use a password in both normal and URL encoded versions, so I guess my best move is to have two vault variables to store the 2 different values?

A workaround was provided in the original report:

```
{{ "{}".format(vaulted_var) | urlencode }}
```
I just stumbled upon this issue after migrating to a new version of ansible. This used to work with ansible 2.9. Are there any plans to fix this issue soon?
